rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-3.3, Figs 3-8, Tables 3-4: the authors run the ISAREG soil-water-balance model with 1970-2005 weather for Pustren vertisol, generating three furrow-irrigation scheduling alternatives plus rainfed, and computing irrigation demand and relative yield decrease for average, very dry and scenario years.
rows.notes: The study does search model-based irrigation schedules to cope with dry years and a pessimistic precipitation scenario, matching the passage topically. However, all results are pure simulation outputs: no schedule, soil-water or yield output of this study is compared with field measurements. Calibration/validation of ISAREG and of the furrow depths come from earlier cited work (Popova et al. 2006a; Popova et al. 1994, 1998), which per the rules does not count as this study's own evidence. Hence Q2 is answered no under the rule that unvalidated model runs do not count; a reader accepting prior validation of the same model on the same site might rate Q2 yes. The study shows that alternatives with MAD 0.47 require less water in average years, alternative 2 (MAD 0.33) has negligible yield loss, all alternatives accommodate the pessimistic scenario mainly by shifting the last irrigation date, and rainfed yield losses rise strongly, especially for the stress-sensitive hybrid. No dispersion statistics or stated limitations of the simulation results beyond noting scenarios are hypothetical and record length is short.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). Single-site (Pustren, one vertisol, one crop with two hybrids) simulation study; climate scenarios are hypothetical trend extrapolations, not predictions, as the authors state.
